skill.name: to-prd
skill.description: Creates a product requirements document from current conversation and codebase context, then publishes it to the project issue tracker.
skill.summary: Creates a PRD from chat context and sends it to the issue tracker.
skill.author: mattpocock

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks mark Markdown inline text around a slash command reference, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md contains no executable code or dynamic command construction at this location.
The backticks mark the literal issue label needs-triage in Markdown. This is documentation text, not a shell command or executable Ruby backtick expression.

content.value_statement: Product plans can lose context when they move from chat to an issue tracker. This skill converts the conversation into a structured PRD and publishes it for triage.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes the current conversation into a product requirements document.
Uses repository context, glossary terms, and ADRs when available.
Sketches major modules that may need implementation or changes.
Prompts for confirmation on module choices and test coverage.
Publishes the PRD to the configured issue tracker with a triage label.
Formats the PRD with problem, solution, user stories, implementation, testing, scope, and notes.
limitations: It depends on the conversation and repository context already available to the agent.
It requires a configured issue tracker and known triage label vocabulary.
It does not perform a full product discovery interview before drafting.
It avoids specific file paths and code snippets in the PRD by design.

use_cases.title: Convert a Planning Chat into a PRD
use_cases.description: Turn an existing product discussion into a structured document ready for team review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Engineering Scope for Triage
use_cases.description: Capture likely modules, implementation decisions, and testing choices before work enters the backlog.

use_cases.title: Document a Feature Before Building
use_cases.description: Create a durable issue from a local design conversation without writing implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a completed feature discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD from our current conversation and publish it to the issue tracker.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Scope and Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning needs testing decisions recorded.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD from this discussion. Include implementation decisions, testing decisions, and clear out-of-scope notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Triage Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the team needs a backlog-ready issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for this feature and publish it with the needs-triage label. Ask me to confirm modules and tests first.

prompt_templates.title: Use Architecture Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for repositories with ADRs and domain vocabulary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PRD for the workflow we discussed. Use the project glossary, respect nearby ADRs, identify deep modules, and confirm test decisions before publishing.

output_examples.input: A conversation about adding team billing controls to an existing SaaS product.
output_examples.output: The skill creates a PRD with customer problems, permission needs, billing workflows, testing areas, and out-of-scope billing changes.

output_examples.input: A refactor discussion about extracting notification delivery into a dedicated module.
output_examples.output: The skill documents the module boundary, user stories, implementation decisions, external behavior tests, and issue tracker triage details.

output_examples.input: A planning session for a search filter improvement across an existing dashboard.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a PRD covering search behavior, UI expectations, data constraints, acceptance context, and deferred enhancements.

best_practices: Provide enough conversation context before running the skill.
Review module and test choices before the PRD is published.
Keep issue tracker setup details current, including labels and permissions.
anti_patterns: Running it before the feature problem is clear.
Using it to replace stakeholder review for high-risk product changes.
Expecting final implementation details when the PRD should stay durable.

faq.question: Does this skill write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It writes a product requirements document and sends it to the issue tracker.

faq.question: Will it ask discovery questions first?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes known context, then asks for module and test confirmation.

faq.question: Can it use repository context?
faq.answer: Yes. It explores the repository when needed and uses project vocabulary and ADRs.

faq.question: Does it include file paths?
faq.answer: No. The template tells the agent to avoid specific file paths and code snippets.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: The project should provide issue tracker details and triage labels before publishing.
